operational_lifespan: 1969-11-19 to 1977-09-30 (8 years, deactivated by NASA command)

central_station.antenna: Modified helical S-band antenna, manually pointed towards Earth using sun compass and elevation gimbal
central_station.thermal_control: Specular aluminum reflector skirt, command-actuated thermal louvers on top plate

snap_27_rtg.casing: Beryllium cylinder with 8 radial heat dissipation fins, height 0.46m, diameter 0.40m
snap_27_rtg.deployment_note: Fuel capsule carried in graphite cask mounted on side of LM descent stage; extracted by Alan Bean using Hanford tool into RTG core

passive_seismic_experiment_pse.purpose: Measure natural lunar seismicity, moonquakes, meteoroid impacts, and artificial spacecraft impacts
passive_seismic_experiment_pse.shroud: Aluminized Mylar / Kapton 10-sided skirt, base diameter 0.9m, for passive thermal protection
key_observations: LM Intrepid ascent stage intentional impact on 1969-11-20 (reverberated for over 60 minutes)
Deep moonquakes occurring cyclically at depths of 800-1000 km triggered by Earth tidal stresses
Recorded footprint impacts and discarded PLSS backpack drops by Conrad and Bean

lunar_surface_magnetometer_lsm.principal_investigator: Dr. Palmer Dyal (NASA Ames Research Center)
lunar_surface_magnetometer_lsm.configuration: Three fluxgate sensors mounted on 1.0m orthogonal boom arms
lunar_surface_magnetometer_lsm.key_result: Discovered permanent crustal remanent magnetic field of ~36 gamma (nT), unexpectedly strong

solar_wind_spectrometer_sws.configuration: Array of 7 Faraday cups oriented upward to capture proton and electron flux from the solar wind

suprathermal_ion_detector_side_ccge.combination: SIDE measures low-energy positive ions; integrated Cold Cathode Gauge Experiment (CCGE) measures ambient lunar atmosphere pressure (down to 10^-12 torr)

lunar_dust_detector.configuration: Three miniature solar photovoltaic cells mounted on top of Central Station to measure dust accumulation from LM liftoff
